title: When the model disagrees most with the market, the market is right
headline_insight: At the widest model-market disagreement (gap >=.10, n=8530 MLB ticks) the model is the closer forecaster only 0.1994 of the time, and its Brier rises to 0.177763 versus the market's 0.129824.
what_it_means: Bucketing predictions by how far the model sits from the market is a direct test of who is right when they disagree. At small disagreements the two are effectively tied on Brier (0.129506 vs 0.129087). But every step up in disagreement, the model gets worse relative to the market -- at the widest gap it lands closer to the truth only about 20% of the time. Large model-market disagreements show the model is wrong.
how_to_read: Each bucket is a disagreement size; a model_closer_rate below 0.5 means the market beats the model in that bucket more often than not.
why_it_matters: It is a hard guardrail against trusting the model's boldest disagreements -- the calls that look most tempting are exactly its weakest.
caveat: The same pattern holds in soccer (model_closer_rate 0.1048 at the widest gap), so it is not an MLB quirk -- though both rest on in-game corpora only.
